a mysterious matter in itself, this book.
So Moshe says: woe, I am the leader of all of
Israel. If You want to destroy them, then in effect
You are destroying me too.
HaShem says to him: "Whoever has sinned against Me,
I will blot him out of My book." You did not sin against
Me, they sinned. Therefore, although I
can exact the price from them,
you are still not connected to the matter, and I will not blot
you out of the book. And you,
"go, lead the people to where I told you," meaning
to the Land of Israel. "Behold, My angel shall go before you,
and on the day I punish, I will punish them for their sin." What is He
saying to him here? Here He tells him that in effect
the angel, the angel of HaShem, and apparently this is the same angel
spoken of in Parashat Mishpatim,
will go before you, to take them, to guide them to
the Land of Israel, "and on the day I punish, I will punish them for their sin."
Then it is written, "And HaShem struck the people for what they did with
the calf that Aharon made." This is at the end of chapter 32. In chapter 33
it is written thus, at the beginning of the chapter: "And HaShem spoke to Moshe:
Go, ascend from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt,
to the land that I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchak and to Yaakov,
saying, 'To your descendants I will give it.' And I will send before you an angel."
Here He repeats the matter once again. He already
said this to him in chapter 32. Now He repeats
it, but this time with the context. See: "And I will send
before you the angel, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite,
the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with
milk and honey." And here is the reason
that I am sending this angel: "for I will not go up
in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way."
And here He says that the angel now is not, as it were,
the expression of the Shechinah in Israel. It is not the angel. It is
not that the angel comes instead, because you are not
worthy of the dwelling of the Shechinah, since I, says HaShem,
will not go up in your midst, and instead of that I am sending
an angel.
That is, there is a distinction here between the angel of Parashat
Mishpatim and of Parashat Beshalach and this angel.
The angel after the calf is an angel who comes in place of
the dwelling of the Shechinah.
"For I will not be in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way."
Therefore it is better that I not be there, and only an angel will be. Moshe
Rabbeinu
does not give up on this matter, and in fact he refuses
to accept this angel, as we will see shortly.
Further on in the chapter, chapter 33, it is written: "And Moshe said
to HaShem: See, You say to me, 'Bring up this people,'
but You have not let me know whom You will send with me." You said
that You would send an angel, but You did not let me know, and we must understand
what He means here by "You have not let me know
whom You will send with me." He told him, I will send an angel,
but there was something unclear here about this angel
that Moshe wants to clarify. "And You have not let me know
whom You will send with me," that is, what is the status of this angel.
"And You said, 'I have known you by name, and also you have found favor
in My eyes.'" Meaning: okay, I told You
that if Israel sinned, then blot me out of Your book. You
said to me, no, you did not sin, therefore I will not blot
you out of Your book. That is, I found favor
in Your eyes. So if I found favor in Your eyes, "let me know." That
is connected to what came before: "You have not let me know whom You will send." So if I found favor in Your eyes, I want
clarification in this matter and in further matters of
understanding the ways of the Creator. "Let me know Your ways,
that I may know You." Why did I find favor in Your eyes? "And see that this nation
is Your people."
And HaShem says to him,
HaShem says to him: "My presence will go
and I will give you rest." What is He saying to him here? This is
a reference to the whole matter of the angel that He is sending
with him, and Moshe wants to understand what the matter is here with the
nature of this angel, and whether the Shechinah really will not
be with us but rather there will be an angel without the Shechinah. This is
the issue under discussion here. And then HaShem
says to him these words: "My presence will go
and I will give you rest." Let us see what Rashi says about this.
"And He said: My presence will go," as Targum renders it:
I will no longer send an angel; I Myself will go, as in "and Your presence
goes in the midst." That is, this was what Moshe
wanted to understand: "And You have not let me know whom You will send with me."
And he says we cannot move from here, as
we will see in a moment, unless we return
to the state in which the Shechinah
is with us. Then HaShem says to him,
okay, indeed you found favor in My eyes, and this is what you
ask, so I restore the situation to what it was. I
Myself will go, and I will no longer send this angel
that I intended to send in place of the Shechinah,
instead of the Shechinah being among Israel. All right? So
this is what he receives here as an answer to his request
that the Shechinah return to dwell in Israel after the calf. "And He said, My presence will go and I will give you rest,"
as Targum renders it: I will no longer send an angel; I Myself will go,
as in "and Your presence goes in the midst." Moshe Rabbeinu says to him
after this, good news, he says to him: yes, certainly,
"And he said to Him: If Your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here." That is,
indeed this is what I want to happen, that You Yourself
be with us, and if not, we are not moving from here. Do not
bring us up from here. "And how then shall it be known that I have found favor
in Your eyes, I and Your people?" You told me earlier that "you have found
favor in My eyes." "Is it not in Your going with us, so that we are distinguished, I
and Your people, from every people on the face of the earth?" And HaShem said
to Moshe: "This thing too that you have spoken I will do, for
you have found favor in My eyes, and I have known you by name," that is, that the Shechinah will be
with Israel, and not that same angel who was supposed to come
in place of the Shechinah.
There is another interesting point that will sharpen what is written
here. Moshe Rabbeinu refuses to accept an angel
instead of HaShem.
Where do we find this thing again? This
angel?
We will find him
at the end of the 40 years, at the entry into the Land. Yes? Moshe
